claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 (deployed 22:00, live at order-processing time) introduced a multi-node east-node-first reservation priority that may be causing split-reservation exceptions on east node lanes.
claims.corroboration: Perfect correlation: 100% of held orders are in scope EXC-0921 (v18 rule-affected orders), and 0% of non-v18 orders are held. Temporal correlation: v18 deployed 22:00, incident orders allocated and held starting 06:00. No other system change (m8_e04 unrelated).
claims.limitation: m8_r_exceptions notes it cannot separate rule-change logic defect from east-node lane specifics. Still need to test whether split-reservation logic is faulty or whether the problem is downstream (carrier feed lag). Regression suite passed but may not have tested split-reservation under new east-node priority.

claims.statement: The east-node-specific carrier pickup feed may have a lag or scheduling gap that prevents carriers from collecting orders that the system believes are ready.
claims.corroboration: Problem is east-node-specific, other nodes normal. Observability gap exists: dashboards do not show booked pickup vs carrier confirmation. Carrier ops reports nothing obvious in dock schedule, but lacks visibility into feed processing.
claims.limitation: Not yet confirmed whether carrier feed received pickup slots for EXC-0921 orders or whether there is a backlog/lag. Need trace of cohort handoff to carrier ops.

claims.statement: Orders are properly allocated and inventoried; the system state is consistent on the fulfillment side.
claims.corroboration: Inventory Control explicitly states allocation totals reconcile and nothing looks wrong on their side.
claims.limitation: Inventory Control cannot see carrier-side records (m8_e09), so reconciliation does not rule out a handoff gap.

contradictions.claim_a: C1: v18 rule logic is defective
contradictions.claim_b: C2: carrier feed has lag/gap, rule change just routed orders there
contradictions.description: Both could be true, but they require different mitigations. If C1 (rule defect), revert_allocation_ruleset is appropriate. If C2 (carrier feed), apply_slot_correction is appropriate. If both, need both mitigations. Currently cannot discriminate.
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: Trace of EXC-0921 cohort handoffs (are orders reaching carrier feed? are slots being booked?). Rule history (did v18 split-reservation logic have known issues or edge cases?). Dock capacity and carrier feed status for east node.

capability_gaps.reason: Need to see whether EXC-0921 orders are stuck in allocation processing, or have reached carrier feed and are stuck there, or are stuck at dock capacity.
Need to establish whether v18's split-reservation logic on east-node has known issues, design flaws, or untested edge cases.

next_action.rationale: Tracing EXC-0921 through the order processing pipeline (allocation → carrier feed → dock) will show exactly where the orders are stuck. This directly discriminates between rule-defect (stuck in allocation) and carrier-feed-lag (stuck after handoff to carrier ops). Combined with review_rule_history, this will establish the root cause.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Very high. Will pinpoint the exact handoff or processing stage where orders are held, and either confirm C1 (rule defect) or point to C2 (carrier feed lag).
